problem_summary.summary: Determine whether a target occurs in a matrix whose rows are sorted and whose row ranges are ordered without overlap.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a nonempty m by n integer matrix and target. Return true if the target appears, otherwise false.
constraints: Rows are non-decreasing and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last value

brute_force.explanation: Inspect every matrix cell and return true as soon as a value equals target; return false after all cells have been checked.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The nested loops visit every valid row-column pair exactly once. Therefore a match is found if and only if target is present.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(m * n), where m and n are the row and column counts.

optimized.explanation: Treat the row-major matrix as one sorted array with indices from 0 to m*n - 1. Convert a flat index i to matrix[i / n][i % n] while doing ordinary binary search.
optimized.correctness_idea: The row-order condition makes the row-major sequence globally sorted. Integer division and remainder map every flat index to its unique matrix cell, so binary search over that sequence is equivalent to searching a sorted array.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log(m * n)) for m rows and n columns.

steps.action: Discard indices through 4 and set left to 5.
Discard indices from 6 onward and set right to 5.

edge_cases.handling: The one-element search interval returns true only when that cell equals target.
The flat-index mapping remains valid in either shape.

edge_cases.case: Target below or above every value
edge_cases.handling: The binary-search interval becomes empty and returns false.

edge_cases.case: Target falls between two adjacent matrix values
edge_cases.handling: The search exhausts the interval and returns false.
